history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION FLAG: The CSV row lists town 'Dhanbad', but no Baidyanath temple is documented anywhere in Dhanbad city — the only documented referent is Baba Baidyanath Dham at Deoghar, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, roughly 107–132 km (2–2.5 hrs by road) from Dhanbad. This file therefore documents the Deoghar temple and corrects town/district to Deoghar; the CSV town entry appears to be an error (keep-or-drop/merge decision needed — note CSV seq 429 is the Deoghar row, so this file may duplicate it). The temple's legend: the demon king Ravana worshipped Shiva here and offered his ten heads; pleased, Shiva healed him, acting as 'Vaidya' (doctor) — hence Vaidyanath. The complex has the main Jyotirlinga shrine plus 21–22 subsidiary shrines of other deities, all said to be built on a single rock; each Shravan month millions of Kanwariyas carry Ganga water on foot from Sultanganj to offer here.

name: Baba Baidyanath Dham
town_description: Deoghar, in the Santhal Parganas of Jharkhand, is one of Hinduism's holiest cities as the home of the Baidyanath Jyotirlinga. It draws millions of pilgrims each year, especially during the Shravan Kanwar Yatra.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi; also Gaya, Patna, Kolkata (no commercial airport at Deoghar town centre)
travel.railway: Jasidih Junction (~7 km); Baidyanathdham station on the Jasidih–Baidyanath Dham branch line
travel.road: On the old GT Road corridor; ~107 km by road from Dhanbad (~2 hrs)

visitor_information.best_time: Avoid Shravan month (June–July) unless doing the pilgrimage — extremely crowded; winter is best
